entries.test: Published research on out-of-distribution generalization in dominant neural network architectures as of 2024.
entries.note: Marcus has made this claim for a long time. 'Trouble' is loose, but most readers would read it as weak out-of-distribution performance.

entries.test: Whether neural models' reasoning and planning failures on benchmarks concentrate on inputs outside their training distribution.
entries.note: A causal claim with a loose measure. It is graded under the lenient default.
The idea that poor generalization drives developers' ethical choices has no shared test. Part of it also rests on developers' motives.
The record adds 'to cover all cases for neural networks', which is more specific than his words. 'Enough' has no stated measure, and 'always be outliers' is close to true by definition.

entries.test: Whether driverless cars were only demos in April 2024, for example whether Waymo was running a paid public robotaxi service then.
entries.note: The factual premise can be checked: Waymo was running paid driverless service in Phoenix and San Francisco by 2024.

entries.test: Whether LLMs reach widely accepted reliability, such as near-zero hallucination and error rates on standard factuality and reasoning evaluations.
entries.note: A 'never' forecast can be refuted but never confirmed. 'Reliable' has no threshold.

entries.test: Published scaling results showing whether gains in performance per unit of added training data shrink as data grows.
entries.note: He states this as his conclusion from the preprint Bupe discussed. 'What we can expect' is a firm expectation, not probability language.
'Not enough' never says enough for what, so readers would test it differently.

entries.test: Whether the data used to train frontier models runs into the available stock of usable human-generated text, as tracked by Epoch AI and others.
entries.note: 'Sooner or later' means there is no deadline.

entries.test: Whether any system widely accepted as AGI is reached by scaling current neural network approaches without new methods for generalization.
entries.note: 'We need' states a necessity, not a moral ought; in effect he predicts that scaling alone will not reach AGI. How AGI is defined will affect any verdict.
